title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Write Ŝ = Ŝ^+_{0,3} for the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3, generated by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). The profinite free group π̂_{0,3} = F̂_2 is the kernel of Ŝ → S_3; it is the completion of Γ(2), with inertia generators l_0, l_1 = ρ(l_0), l_∞ = ρ²(l_0), where ρ(x) means conjugation by ρ. The goal (stated as a theorem on the next page) is to describe automorphisms of π̂_{0,3}, as a 'groupe étoile' (with its inertia classes), that commute with the S_3 action. One realises them as automorphisms u of Ŝ that fix σ_∞, send ρ to gρ with g in π̂_{0,3}, and preserve the conjugacy class of the closed subgroup L_0' = <l_0'>, where l_0' = ε_0 = σ_∞ρ and l_0 = l_0'^2. The data are an element g_0 (written q_0 on this page) and γ, with g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1}.

Step 1 (eq. 44). The previous page computed int(g_0^{-1}) u(ε_0) = ε_0^{2γ+1}. Hence u(l_0') = int(g_0)(l_0'^p) with p = 2γ+1. Squaring gives (39): u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^p). So the inertia at 0 is sent to a conjugate of its p-th power, and p is the cyclotomic-type multiplier.

Step 2 (NB). Conversely, if p ∈ Ẑ^*, then (p-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ. This is checked prime by prime: for ℓ ≠ 2, 2 is a unit in Z_ℓ; for ℓ = 2, p ≡ 1 or 3 mod 4, so p-1 is even in Z_2. So γ = (p-1)/2 is well defined.

Step 3 (eqs. 45-46). The order-3 condition (38), (gρ)^3 = 1, i.e. g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, is expanded:
σ(q) l_1^γ ρ(q^{-1}) · ρσ(q) l_∞^γ ρ²(q^{-1}) · ρ²σ(q) l_0^γ q^{-1} = 1.
The adjacent factors telescope into ρ^i(q^{-1}σ(q)). Conjugating by q^{-1} and setting h_0 = σ_∞(q_0)^{-1} q_0 = [σ_∞, q_0^{-1}] gives
h_0^{-1} l_1^γ ρ(h_0^{-1}) l_∞^γ ρ²(h_0^{-1}) l_0^γ = 1.
Conjugating by l_0^γ, and using l_1 = ρ(l_0) and l_∞ = ρ²(l_0), this becomes f ρ(f) ρ²(f) = 1 with f = l_0^γ h_0^{-1} and γ = (p-1)/2. This is the boxed (46), identified with an earlier condition (10); another earlier condition (7) is declared superfluous.

In modern terms, (46) is exactly the Drinfeld/Ihara 'hexagon' (relation II) of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, f(x,y) x^m f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m = 1 with m = (λ-1)/2, up to the convention of where the l^γ factors sit. The 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 is built in by the parametrisation h_0 = σ(q)^{-1} q: σ(h_0) = h_0^{-1} automatically. The page therefore derives the genus-0, three-point part of the GT definition (relations I and II with m = (λ-1)/2) from S_3-equivariance plus inertia-preservation, using the PSL_2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 presentation.
errors: No genuine mathematical error found. The derivation is correct once one reads ρ(x) as conjugation by ρ, with l_1 = ρ(l_0) and l_∞ = ρ²(l_0).
Minor: in the expanded form of (38), the middle factor must end with ρ²(q_0^{-1}), not ρ(q_0^{-1}). The handwriting is ambiguous; the telescoping only works with ρ².
Minor logical point: p = 2γ+1 is not automatically a unit for an arbitrary γ ∈ Ẑ. The NB handles the converse direction (p ∈ Ẑ^* ⇒ γ ∈ Ẑ); invertibility of p comes from u being an automorphism.
Notation drift: the element is written q_0 on this page and g_0 on the adjacent pages.

ideas.what: Describing S_3-equivariant, inertia-preserving automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} = F̂_2 as automorphisms of the completed PSL_2(Z) = Z/2*Z/3 that fix σ_∞ and send ρ to gρ
ideas.modern_name: Profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group ĜT (genus 0, 3 points) via the PSL_2(Z)/Γ(2) presentation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); the PSL_2(Z)-type viewpoint appears in Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981) discuss Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on π̂_{0,3} and the Teichmüller tower, but not, to my knowledge, these explicit relations

ideas.what: Relation f ρ(f) ρ²(f) = 1 with f = l_0^γ h_0^{-1} and γ = (p-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld–Ihara hexagon relation (relation II of GT) with m = (λ-1)/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: V. Drinfeld 1990 (On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras...), Y. Ihara 1991

ideas.what: Parametrising the cocycle as h_0 = σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g_0 = [σ_∞, g_0^{-1}], so the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 holds automatically
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary-type parametrisation of solutions of GT relation I
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (similar 'f = g(y,x)^{-1} g(x,y)' observations appear in the GT literature)

ideas.what: Inertia exponent λ odd in Ẑ^*, so (λ-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ; checked ℓ-adically

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly derives the hexagon relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, with exponent γ = (p-1)/2, from S_3-equivariance plus preservation of the inertia class. He uses the presentation of completed PSL_2(Z) as generated by σ_∞ and ρ with σ_∞² = (gρ)³ = 1. These notes continue La Longue Marche (1981), which would place this derivation years before Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1991).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority and history of GT. The literature credits the defining relations of ĜT to Drinfeld and Ihara, and treats Grothendieck as having only programmatically suggested such a group. If the dating holds, this page shows he had the relations explicitly, together with the PSL_2(Z) mechanism behind them.

missed.claim: Relation I comes for free from writing h_0 = [σ_∞, g_0^{-1}] in terms of a 'half' g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0. The full data are thus (p, g_0 mod L_0) subject to one relation plus a generation condition, a slightly different parametrisation of ĜT than Drinfeld's (λ, f).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This parametrisation via an element defined modulo the inertia subgroup L_0 could be compared with known descriptions of ĜT inside Out(completed PSL_2(Z)) and with the 'one-relation' results (Furusho-type) on GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation itself is short and correct. But it shows Grothendieck writing down, in explicit form, the GT hexagon relation with m = (λ-1)/2, derived from the Z/2*Z/3 presentation, in notes apparently from the early 1980s, before Drinfeld and Ihara. That is a notable unpublished detail; dating uncertainty keeps the score moderate.
transcription_corrections: Throughout this page 'q_0' is the same element written g_0 on the neighbouring pages.
In the expansion of (38), the second underbraced factor should read ρσ_∞(q_0) l_∞^γ ρ²(q_0^{-1}) (exponent 2 on ρ), as the telescoping requires.
'd'où (39), en élevant au carré' is the likely reading of the line after (44), not 'en éliminant au carré'.
In (46), the first factor is (l_0^γ h_0^{-1}), not (l_0^γ h_0^{-1}) with l_∞; all three factors use l_0^γ.
